articles.title: [18F]FDG‑PET/CT screening in infective endocarditis detects both symptomatic and asymptomatic extracardiac lesions of clinical relevance.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Extracardiac complications (ECC) influence prognosis and management in infective endocarditis (IE) substantially. Although [18F]FDG-PET/CT is recommended for symptomatic patients, the value in unselected IE populations remains uncertain. METHODS: Retrospective multicenter study evaluating consecutive patients with suspected or definite IE undergoing [18F]FDG-PET/CT screening in the Region of Southern Denmark (January-August 2025). Extracardiac findings were registered per-lesion. Clinical impact was defined as any downstream consequence attributable to a [18F]FDG-PET/CT-detected lesion, irrespective of the clinical relevance. Significant clinical impact required a clinically relevant lesion affecting patient management. RESULTS: Extracardiac lesions were detected in 120/152 patients with clinical impact in 61 and significant clinical impact in 34 (39 lesions), corresponding to a number needed to screen of 4-5. Of the 39 lesions with significant clinical impact, 18 were symptomatic and 21 asymptomatic, including malignancies, visceral septic embolism, and drainable foci. Vertebral infection was suspected in 15 patients and confirmed in 13; only 2 lacked prescan back pain, indicating that [18F]FDG-PET/CT rarely identifies asymptomatic spondylodiscitis. In contrast, among 15 patients infected with gut-associated streptococci, [18F]FDG-PET/CT revealed colonic foci in 8 asymptomatic cases, all leading to polypectomy, thereby removing a lesion that may have been relevant to the pathogenesis of IE. CONCLUSION: Systematic [18F]FDG-PET/CT screening generated substantial subsequent diagnostic workload with limited clinical value, as lesions affecting patient management were detected in only a minority. Half of these occurred in patients without prescan symptoms, thereby raising the possibility that [18F]FDG-PET/CT may have a role in specific asymptomatic subgroups beyond the guideline‑recommended symptom‑driven application.

articles.title: 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT was complemented by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT for benign insulinoma imaging, with histopathology validation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the role of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and the histopathology analysis in patients with suspected insulinoma. METHODS: 100 patients with suspected insulinoma were enrolled. Diagnostic performance, semi-quantitative parameter values, and immunoreactivity score (IRS) were compared. Correlation of GLP-1R and SSTR2 IRS was analyzed with semi-quantitative parameters, maximum tumor diameter, and Ki-67 index. RESULTS: 51 patients and 11 patients were confirmed as insulinoma with histopathology and consensus of the multidisciplinary team (MDT), respectively. The combination of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT achieved superior diagnostic performance, reducing false-negative results compared to single-tracer PET/CT. The dual-tracer PET/CT demonstrated higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value (NPV) than 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 (NPV, p < 0.05) and 68Ga-DOTATATE (all p < 0.001). In G1 lesions, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showed significantly higher SUVmax (49.55 ± 37.69 vs. 22.46 ± 14.38, p = 0.035) and TBR (12.38 ± 6.55 vs. 6.71 ± 4.59, p = 0.029) than 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT. These results were in accordance with elevated SSTR2 IRS compared with GLP-1R IRS (8.60 ± 1.92 vs. 6.01 ± 1.87, p = 0.002). In G2 lesions, SUVmax, TBR, and GLP-1R IRS were slightly higher on 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT (p > 0.05). SSTR2 IRS was positively associated with maximum tumor diameter (r = 0.358, p = 0.025) and negatively associated with the Ki-67 index (r = -0.547, p < 0.001). SUVmax and TBR of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showed positive correlations with their corresponding IRS (all p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT is recommended as the first-line functional imaging modality for patients with suspected insulinoma. When 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT shows negative results, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT serves a complementary role. These were in accordance with the different expression of GLP-1R and SSTR2 between G1 and G2 insulinomas.

articles.title: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT in stage IV non-small cell lung cancer undergoing immune checkpoint blockade: Comparison to [18F]FDG PET/CT and role in response evaluation and prognosis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT and [18F]FDG PET/CT in patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and to explore the potential of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-derived parameters in evaluating treatment response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), as well as the association between total lesion (TL) FAPI and progression-free survival (PFS). METHODS: Twenty patients with stage IV NSCLC were prospectively included in this exploratory study. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT was performed at baseline and repeated after six weeks of ICB therapy. Baseline lesion uptake (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and target-to-background ratio (TBR)) were compared with previously performed [18F]FDG PET/CT. Baseline values and early changes in [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-derived parameters (ΔTLFAPI and primary tumour ΔSUVmax) were related to treatment response and evaluated in relation to PFS. RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT demonstrated a higher TBR than [18F]FDG PET/CT (all lesions analysed together: median TBR 7.34 vs. 5.05; p < 0.01), while SUVmax values did not differ significantly (median 9.42 vs. 9.13; p = 0.06). Early treatment responders showed marked reductions in TLFAPI whereas non-responders showed a median increase (median change - 50.41% vs. +10.11%; p = 0.01). Above-median baseline TLFAPI was associated with shorter PFS (HR 3.33, 95% CI 1.01-10.96; p = 0.048). CONCLUSION: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT confirmed its potential role in lesion detection. This exploratory study showed that early changes in TLFAPI might be associated with treatment response of ICB, and that baseline TLFAPI might be associated with PFS. Future studies on the role of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT in guiding ICB therapy would be of great interest.

articles.title: Threshold optimization of artificial intelligence in digital breast tomosynthesis screening: a retrospective comparison study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of a deep learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) system for digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) screening and to compare its performance with radiologist-plus-CAD interpretation across multiple operating thresholds. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 1780 asymptomatic women who underwent screening DBT between July 2021 and June 2022. Radiologists interpreted examinations using BI-RADS, 5th edition; the AI system independently analyzed the examinations. Three operating thresholds were assessed: high-sensitivity threshold (HST) (≥ 2%), Youden index threshold (YIT) (≥ 27%), and recall rate-matched threshold (RMT) (≥ 36%). The reference standard was histopathologic confirmation for positive cases and a 24-month follow-up for negative cases. Sensitivity, specificity, and recall rates were compared using the McNemar test. RESULTS: Among 1780 women (mean age ± SD, 55.7 ± 7.4 years), 1469 (82.5%) had dense breasts (BI-RADS density category C or D). Eighteen cancers were confirmed: 12 screen-detected and 6 interval cancers (cancer rate in the cohort, 10.1 per 1000 examinations). At the YIT (≥ 27%), AI achieved numerically higher sensitivity than radiologist-plus-CAD (77.8% (14/18) vs 66.7% (12/18)), although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.457), with lower specificity (81.2% vs 95.2%; p < 0.001) and a higher recall rate (19.4% vs 5.4%; p < 0.001). Negative predictive value (NPV) was high for both (99.7% vs 99.6%). AI detected two of six interval cancers missed by radiologist-plus-CAD; four interval cancers were missed by both methods. CONCLUSION: Standalone AI performance was threshold-dependent, with numerically higher sensitivity but significantly lower specificity than radiologist-plus-CAD, requiring external validation given the limited sample. KEY POINTS: Question What is the optimal threshold for standalone artificial intelligence in digital breast tomosynthesis screening to balance cancer detection and recall rates? Findings Standalone artificial intelligence showed numerically higher sensitivity but significantly lower specificity than radiologist-plus-CAD (81.2% vs 95.2%), with threshold choice shaping detection and recall. Clinical relevance In digital breast tomosynthesis screening, standalone AI performance varied with the selected threshold. At the Youden threshold, AI maintained a high negative predictive value and detected 2 of 6 interval cancers; the small cancer sample limits conclusions about clinical benefit.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of MR arthrography for detecting adhesions after arthroscopic hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of MR arthrography for detecting postoperative intra-articular adhesions after hip arthroscopy (HAS) for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAIS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients undergoing hip MR arthrography from February 2015 through December 2025, followed by revision HAS within 180 days. Three radiologists independently assessed capsulofemoral and perilabral adhesions using predefined morphologic criteria. Two radiologists independently classified anterior and superolateral capsular distension as substantial or limited based on capsular convexity and contrast-filled separation from the femoral neck, respectively. Sensitivity, specificity, positive/negative predictive values, and accuracy with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using revision arthroscopy as the reference standard. Interreader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC2. RESULTS: Among 62 patients (mean age, 39 ± 9 years; 31 women), arthroscopy identified adhesions in 41 (66%), including capsulofemoral adhesions in 35 (56%) and perilabral adhesions in 17 (27%). Across readers, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 78-80%, 62-76%, and 73-77% for any adhesion; 71-77%, 63-81%, and 68-77% for capsulofemoral adhesions; and 65-76%, 80-87%, and 76-81% for perilabral adhesions, respectively. Interreader agreement was good and very good for capsulofemoral and perilabral adhesions (κ = 0.65 and 0.83, respectively). With substantial capsular distension, specificity and accuracy were numerically higher at 77-91% and 76-88% for capsulofemoral adhesions and 85-95% and 78-85% for perilabral adhesions, respectively. CONCLUSION: The diagnostic performance observed in our study supports the use of MR arthrography for the preoperative evaluation of suspected adhesions after HAS for FAIS, with good to very good interreader agreement for the assessment of capsulofemoral and perilabral adhesions. KEY POINTS: Question What is the diagnostic performance of MR arthrography for detecting postoperative adhesions in patients with persistent symptoms after arthroscopic surgery for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome? Findings Across three readers, MR arthrography demonstrated accuracies of 68-77% for capsulofemoral adhesions and 76-81% for perilabral adhesions, with good to very good interreader agreement. Clinical relevance MR arthrography supports preoperative evaluation of suspected adhesions in symptomatic patients after arthroscopic treatment of femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, providing clinically relevant diagnostic information for further management and revision arthroscopy planning.

articles.title: Post-TIPS prediction via multimodal interaction: A multi-center dataset and framework for survival, complication, and portal pressure assessment.
articles.abstract: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is an established procedure for portal hypertension, which provides variable survival outcomes and leads to frequent overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE), indicating the necessity of accurate preoperative prognostic modeling. Current studies typically build machine learning models from preoperative computed tomography (CT) images or clinical characteristics, but face three key challenges: (1) labor-intensive region-of-interest (ROI) annotation, (2) poor reliability and generalizability of unimodal methods, and (3) incomplete assessment from single-endpoint prediction. Moreover, the lack of publicly accessible datasets constrains its research. Therefore, we present MultiTIPS, the first public multi-center dataset for TIPS prognosis, and propose a novel multimodal prognostic framework, comprising three core modules: (1) Dual-option segmentation, which integrates semi-supervised and foundation model-based pipelines to achieve robust ROI segmentation under limited annotations and facilitate feature extraction; (2) Multimodal interaction, where multi-grained radiomics attention (MGRA), progressive orthogonal disentanglement (POD), and clinically guided prognostic enhancement (CGPE) are integrated to enable cross-modal feature interaction and complementary representation, thus improving model accuracy and robustness; (3) Multi-task prediction, where a staged training strategy is used to perform stable optimization of survival, portal pressure gradient (PPG), and OHE prediction for comprehensive prognostic assessment. Extensive experiments on MultiTIPS demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over state-of-the-art approaches, along with cross-domain generalization and interpretability, indicating its promise for clinical application. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/djh-dzxw/TIPS_master.

articles.title: Dual-domain regularized deep unrolled MR fingerprinting reconstruction using structural and spatial constraints.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is a promising quantitative imaging technique for simultaneous multi-parametric tissue characterization. Existing MRF reconstruction methods primarily rely on characteristics of the matricized/tensorized MRF data. However, the underlying nonlinear structural information in the fingerprint domain is not fully exploited, and the tissue parameter domain priors also remain underutilized, which limits further improvements in imaging accuracy. In this paper, we propose a novel dual-domain regularized deep unrolled framework for MRF reconstruction, by jointly enforcing the geometric structure priors of the fingerprints and the spatial constraints of the parameter maps. We first generalize the manifold structure priors to a wider range of Lp norms, allowing diverse formulations that can be finely tuned for the specific reconstruction task to improve reconstruction quality. In addition, we incorporate sparsity regularization on parameter maps to further enhance the quantification performance. To efficiently solve the reconstruction problem, we cast the overall iterative procedure into deep network form. Specifically, we propose a learnable p-norm enhanced manifold structure regularization module to enable data-driven adaptability in structural prior representations across different reconstruction scenarios. We also propose a learned sparsity module equipped with an attention-based soft-thresholding operator to enforce the sparsity constraints of the parameter maps. Experimental results on both simulated and in vivo datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art methods.

articles.title: Glymphatic dysfunction links neuropsychiatric symptoms to cognitive decline via neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPSs) are prevalent in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the mechanistic link to glymphatic dysfunction remains unclear. METHODS: In this multi-cohort study (Chinese discovery cohort, n = 212; Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative [ADNI; n = 446]), NPSs were assessed via the Neuropsychiatric Inventory Questionnaire (NPI-Q) and categorized into hyperactivity, psychosis, affective, and apathy subsyndromes. The diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index was used as a noninvasive imaging proxy related to glymphatic function. Cross-sectional associations of NPSs with ALPS-index, cognition, brain structures, and positron emission tomography (PET) measures (ADNI only) were examined. In ADNI, longitudinal trajectories were evaluated by NPSs-ALPS phenotypes, followed by exploratory survival analyses of cognitive progression and amyloid conversion. Mediation analyses examined whether ALPS-index and neurodegeneration mediated the NPSs-cognition association. A multivariable Cox nomogram incorporating NPI-Q score, ALPS-index, APOE ε4 status, and demographics was developed and internally validated for cognitive progression. RESULTS: NPSs, particularly apathy subsyndrome, were associated with lower ALPS-index, poorer cognition, and brain atrophy across cohorts. In ADNI, NPSs were additionally associated with AD-related PET pathology. Lower ALPS-index and brain atrophy/PET pathology, individually or jointly, mediated the NPSs-cognition association. Longitudinally, the NPSs + Low_ALPS phenotype showed greater cognitive and neuroimaging deterioration and higher risks of cognitive progression (HR = 2.63) and amyloid conversion (HR = 6.17) than the non-NPSs + High_ALPS phenotype. Similar patterns were observed for Apathy-ALPS phenotypes. The nomogram showed acceptable discrimination for cognitive progression. CONCLUSIONS: Lower ALPS-index values, reflecting altered glymphatic function, may link NPSs with cognitive decline through neurodegenerative changes in AD. Integrating NPSs with the ALPS-index could provide complementary information for characterizing disease progression and risk stratification.

articles.title: Evaluation of hematological toxicity of lutetium-177 DOTATATE treatment in patients with advanced neuroendocrine tumors and extensive bone metastases.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with 177Lu-DOTATATE has transformed the treatment for advanced gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NETs). However, hematological toxicity and treatment-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MN), remains a concern particularly in patients with extensive bone metastases. This study aimed to evaluate the hematological safety of 177Lu-DOTATATE PRRT in patients with advanced NETs and extensive bone metastases. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed Mayo Clinic patients with > 50% skeletal involvement by positron emission tomography DOTATATE, who were treated with 177Lu-DOTATATE. Patients were classified into "confluent" or "extensive" bone metastases based on the extent of bone involvement. Clinical data and laboratory results before, during, and after treatment were collected. Hematological toxicity was graded per NCI-CTCAE v5. RESULTS: Between 2017 and 2023, 550 patients underwent PRRT, 48 of whom met inclusion criteria. The median number of PRRT cycles was 4 (range 1-8) with a median cumulative dose of 29.6 GBq. Median follow up was 15.7 months. Four patients required dose reductions due to renal dysfunction, and one due to hematological toxicity. Twenty-four patients (50%) experienced hematological toxicity of any grade, with 14 (29%) developing grade 3/4 toxicity (thrombocytopenia 19%, anemia 14.5%, neutropenia 10%). Ten patients (21%) had persistent cytopenias six months post-PRRT. One patient (2%) developed myelodysplastic syndrome and 2 had clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance (4%). CONCLUSIONS: In this large institutional series, PRRT was associated with moderate but mostly transient grade 3/4 hematological toxicity in patients with advanced NETs and extensive/confluent bone metastases. PRRT should be considered in this patient subgroup, while emphasizing the need for vigilant monitoring of hematological toxicity.

articles.title: Carotid plaque inflammation on [18F]FDG PET/MR provides incremental prognostic information beyond Plaque-RADS and luminal stenosis in medically treated atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether carotid plaque inflammation quantified by [18F]FDG PET/MR-derived target-to-background ratio (TBR) provides incremental prognostic information beyond luminal stenosis and MRI-based Carotid Plaque-RADS for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events in medically treated carotid atherosclerosis. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 151 patients with carotid atherosclerosis receiving medical therapy who underwent baseline [18F]FDG PET/MR. SUVmax, TBR, Plaque-RADS, and stenosis severity were assessed with readers blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was three-point MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal ischaemic stroke. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated using Cox regression, time-dependent ROC analysis, bootstrap-validated Harrell C-index, AIC, likelihood ratio testing, and continuous net reclassification improvement. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 36 months (IQR 32-41 months), 21 patients (13.9%) experienced three-point MACE. After adjustment for age, sex, and C-reactive protein, TBR (HR 5.10, 95% CI 3.22-8.07), SUVmax (HR 4.03, 2.21-7.35), stenosis severity (HR 8.54, 3.84-18.97), and Plaque-RADS (HR 4.19, 1.73-10.15) were each associated with MACE. Addition of TBR to a structural model comprising stenosis and Plaque-RADS yielded the highest discrimination (apparent C-index 0.911; optimism-corrected 0.906) and lowest AIC (147.49). TBR showed higher 36-month discrimination than SUVmax (AUC 0.94 vs. 0.80). CONCLUSION: In medically treated patients with carotid atherosclerosis, [18F]FDG PET/MR-derived TBR was associated with three-point MACE and provided incremental prognostic information beyond MRI-based Plaque-RADS and luminal stenosis.

articles.title: Reduced versus standard activity regimens in [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer: efficacy and toxicity profiling.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Lutetium-177 ([177Lu]Lu)-Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) using reduced vs. standard activity regimens. METHODS: In this exploratory retrospective single-center study, 55 patients scheduled for a reduced activity regimen of 6 GBq [177Lu]Lu-PSMA per cycle were compared with 55 receiving standard activity (7.4 GBq per cycle). Efficacy was assessed by Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) changes after two cycles using Prostate Cancer Clinical Working Group version 3 (PCWG3), progression-free (PFS), and overall survival (OS). We also stratified patients into low- vs. high-PSMA-tumor volume (TV) groups determined by baseline PSMA PET/CT. Toxicity was assessed by evaluating laboratory changes from baseline to nadir, along with Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events (AE) 5.0. RESULTS: Reduced activity RPT was effective with a median PSA change of -32% (Interquartile range, -78 to 42%) after two cycles. 25 patients (45%) achieved partial response (stable disease: 14 (25%); progressive disease: 16 (29%)). PSA change (P = 0.961), PCWG3 response distributions (P ≥ 0.219), PFS (P = 0.449) and OS (P = 0.096) were similar in both activity groups. For the reduced activity regimen, we observed significant increase in creatinine (+ 5%) and declines in hemoglobin (-13%), white blood cell counts (-24%) and platelets (-26%; P ≤ 0.001). Those differences, however, were comparable relative to the standard activity group (P ≥ 0.135). In a similar manner, number of renal and hematologic grade 3 AE were identical in both cohorts (six, each). CONCLUSION: In this preliminary, retrospective proof-of-concept analysis, reduced-activity [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT was associated with encouraging efficacy and safety outcomes compared with standard-activity treatment. These hypothesis-generating findings may provide a preliminary rationale for future prospective studies evaluating the clinical utility of individualized activity regimens in PSMA RPT.

articles.title: Bone tumours with wash-out on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI: beyond giant cell tumour of bone.
articles.abstract: Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI is a well-known technique to characterise perfusion in bone tumours, yet the diagnostic value of the wash-out phenomenon-rapid peak enhancement followed by a decline in signal intensity-remains underappreciated in musculoskeletal imaging. Wash-out is characteristic of giant cell tumours of bone, and this enhancement pattern may aid both diagnosis and treatment response assessment. This critical review summarises current applications of DCE-MRI in bone tumours, explains its principles, and highlights key findings from recent literature. We based our results on a systematic literature search in PubMed performed in March 2025, using these keywords: (1) magnetic resonance imaging, (2) bone tumour, (3) perfusion/wash-out, and added relevant MeSH terms and synonyms. We identified nineteen different bone tumour entities for which time-intensity curves were shown. Tumours with wash-out were either benign or malignant, including osteosarcoma, multiple myeloma, bone metastases of several primary tumours, and rare neoplasms such as epithelioid haemangioma or Erdheim-Chester disease. Notably, wash-out does not reliably distinguish benign from malignant lesions due to overlapping perfusion characteristics. We highlighted the clinical utility of DCE-MRI in narrowing differential diagnoses, monitoring treatment response, and detecting recurrence, particularly in complex postoperative scenarios. We observed significant heterogeneity in time-intensity curve classification and interpretation between different studies. In summary, wash-out is an advanced MRI feature that occurs across a diverse spectrum of primary and metastatic bone tumours. Greater awareness of wash-out patterns beyond giant cell tumour of bone may serve to enhance diagnostic confidence, especially in challenging cases. KEY POINTS: Question We critically reviewed the literature on wash-out (dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) variable) in bone tumours to give an overview of entities demonstrating this perfusion characteristic. Findings Wash-out is not exclusive to giant cell tumour of bone and occurs in both benign and malignant primary bone tumours and in metastases. Critical relevance statement Wash-out on DCE-MRI is a valuable diagnostic feature present in a diverse spectrum of primary bone tumours and bone metastases. Greater awareness of wash-out patterns can enhance diagnostic confidence and help assess treatment response or tumour recurrence in challenging cases.

Effects of MR Sampling on Object Detection.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To provide a framework relating resolution and k-space sampling to human detection of objects and a new signal-to-noise metric more directly related to detection. THEORY AND METHODS: An analytic form to predict detectability of an object dependent on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), resolution, and sampling trajectory was proposed. A perception task and detection task were generated using images with synthetic noise. RESULTS: Subjects selected images to be perceptually more similar if they had the same SNR using the new metric rather than the conventional metric. Subjects had greater accuracy of detecting circles when looking at images simulating noise from non-Cartesian images. A detectability threshold using the new SNR metric was optimized to determine the minimum SNR and object size necessary to be detected. CONCLUSION: The new SNR metric may be more directly related to perception and detection. The framework may be useful in predicting object detection from arbitrary sampling trajectories.

articles.title: Tradeoff tuning via continuous organ-at-risk priority input for AI-Generated intensity-modulated radiation therapy plans for head-and-neck cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In current clinical practice, tradeoffs in treatment planning are handled by using multi-criteria optimization (MCO) algorithms or manual operations; very few AI models are capable of handling tradeoffs. PURPOSE: To design an Artificial Intelligence (AI) system that generates fluence maps with tunable tradeoffs, and to examine its performance in head-and-neck (HN) intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) treatment. METHODS: User-tunable, continuous organ-at-risk (OAR) priorities were conditioned into an AI-driven auto-planning system that predicts fluence maps for IMRT plans. Two separate AI models were developed and assembled sequentially for the auto-planning process. The first model predicted individual IMRT field dose using anatomy, tradeoff preferences, and beam configurations as inputs, followed by the second model that generated fluence maps. The two models were trained independently before being integrated for automatic plan generation. A total of 230 patients were included in this study (200/5/25 for training/validation/testing). Two IMRT plans were generated for each training case. One used a set of original priorities adopted from clinical planning template that had balanced dose tradeoffs among OARs and planning target volume (PTV); the other used the same set of dose-volume objectives while OAR sparing priorities were randomly altered by up to ± 20%. To examine the AI system's performance, three tests were designed to examine AI plans with a wide range of OAR priorities under different clinical scenarios. RESULTS: All AI plans using original OAR priorities have clinically acceptable dose distributions. As the OAR priorities change, dose distributions and dose volume histograms (DVHs) in the AI plans change accordingly within the -40% to +80% adjustment range. The dose metrics in AI plans have monotonic response to the corresponding input priorities, with high priorities achieving more sparing. Subtle secondary dose tradeoffs among OARs are also observed. CONCLUSIONS: The AI system can generate substantially different AI plans for the same patient according to the OAR sparing priority input. The AI-predicted fluence maps are computationally efficient, making intuitive tradeoff tuning real-time. Further, this study demonstrates the promising performance of the AI system beyond traditional inverse planning loop and may potentially enhance AI's adoption in clinical planning process.

articles.title: Leadership and Business Training in Radiology.
articles.abstract: In the modern healthcare environment, radiologists increasingly face responsibilities that extend beyond image interpretation and patient care. Changes in reimbursement models, rapid technological advances, and growing demands for operational efficiency have made leadership, financial management, strategic planning, and negotiation skills increasingly important, particularly for those seeking administrative and academic roles. Formal business education, including the Master of Business Administration (MBA), represents one pathway for developing these competencies, while complementary approaches include institutional leadership roles, professional society programs, mentorship, and practical experience. This Perspective examines the potential value of business education in radiology, reviews available evidence on its professional benefits, and discusses educational pathways across career stages, including the application of strategic frameworks and financial principles to radiology practice.

articles.title: Feasibility of Multiparametric Chest MRI in Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility and interobserver reproducibility of a noncontrast multiparametric chest magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocol in patients with connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), and to assess its association with computed tomography (CT)-based quantitative fibrosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 28 patients with CTD-ILD underwent noncontrast chest MRI including ultrashort echo-time (UTE) lung imaging, pulmonary trunk flow, cine ventricular function, and lung T2 mapping. Three blinded thoracic radiologists independently assessed MR-visible pulmonary fibrosis. Interobserver agreement for MR-visible fibrosis was evaluated. Exploratory analyses assessed the agreement between MR-visible fibrosis, CT-based quantitative fibrosis (QILD), and pulmonary function tests. RESULTS: All 28 patients completed the planned MRI protocol (100%). Interpretable images were obtained in all patients for pulmonary trunk flow and cine ventricular imaging, and in 27 of 28 patients (96.4%) for UTE lung imaging and lung T2 mapping. The mean total scan time was 56.9 ±13.2 minutes. The proportion of patients with MR-visible fibrosis ranged from 81.5% to 96.3% across readers, notably higher than the CT-quantified disease burden in this cohort (median QILD, 1.2%). Interobserver agreement was fair to moderate across features (Fleiss' κ = 0.357-0.488). The extent of MR-visible fibrosis demonstrated a significant positive correlation with QILD (Spearman ρ = 0.568, P = 0.002). Lung T2 mapping values also correlated positively with QILD (ρ = 0.591, P = 0.001). CONCLUSION: Noncontrast multiparametric chest MRI is feasible in patients with CTD-ILD, providing interpretable lung and cardiopulmonary imaging within a single examination. Interobserver agreement for MR-visible fibrosis was fair to moderate, and fibrosis extent and T2 mapping values correlated with CT-based quantitative fibrosis, supporting further investigation of MRI as a radiation-sparing imaging option, pending longitudinal validation, in CTD-ILD.

articles.title: Semi-automated Quantitative Assessment of Radiology Resident Reporting Performance Using Large Language Models: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate a semi-automated large language model (LLM)-based scoring pipeline to quantify diagnostic agreement between radiology residents' preliminary and expert-validated final reports. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty-eight paired reports from six radiology residents at a single-center were processed through a two-step pipeline: LLM-based data extraction followed by expert validation and LLM scoring. GPT-5 served as the primary model with full intra-rater and inter-rater reproducibility analyses (35 and 68 pairs, respectively); GPT-4 served as the secondary model. Three metrics were computed: Global Obtained Score (GOS), Global Expected Score (GES), and Clinical Similarity Index (CSI). Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC, two-way random, absolute agreement) and Bland-Altman analysis. A discordance review was performed on 22 report pairs with absolute CSI differences >0.10. RESULTS: GPT-5 achieved good-to-excellent intra-rater reproducibility (ICC: GOS 0.91, GES 0.99, CSI 0.88), comparable to expert scoring (0.93, 0.98, 0.82). Agreement between GPT-5 and the expert was good for GOS (ICC 0.88), excellent for GES (0.98), and moderate-to-good for CSI (0.75). CSI agreement improved from ICC 0.52 (GPT-4) to 0.75 (GPT-5), with a 28% reduction in Bland-Altman limits of agreement. Inter-human agreement on a discordant-enriched subset was moderate to good (ICC: GOS 0.83, GES 0.85, CSI 0.71). Discordance analysis identified five recurring error categories and one hallucination. In 7/30 (23.3%) reviewed disagreements, the expert retrospectively agreed with GPT-5 scoring, including clinically impactful discrepancies initially overlooked during expert scoring. CONCLUSION: The proposed framework provides a structured and reproducible approach for quantitative assessment of radiology resident reporting performance. These preliminary findings support feasibility and warrant larger multicenter validation before educational deployment.

articles.title: Dual Energy Photon-Counting Detector CT for Spinal Bone Marrow Edema Imaging.
articles.abstract: Photon-counting detector (PCD) CT is an emerging technology with several applications in neuroradiology. In the spine, most recent studies have focused on detection of spinal CSF leaks and vascular imaging, largely because these applications benefit from high spatial resolution. However, PCD CT also confers inherent spectral sensitivity that may support additional applications. Spectral applications of PCD CT have been less extensively described, with prior uses including reduction in metallic hardware artifact and accentuation of contrast attenuation for spinal CSF leak detection. One potential use that has not yet been detailed is the detection of bone marrow edema to help characterize the age and healing status of vertebral body compression fractures. PCD CT has the unique ability to perform material decomposition by using spectral information both from the PCD's intrinsic energy-resolving capabilities and from the use of dual-energy acquisition. This functionality may be particularly useful for bone marrow edema imaging, which is a relatively more complex material decomposition task. In this technical report, we describe specific scanning and reconstruction parameters on PCD CT to perform dual-source, dual-kV bone marrow edema imaging in the spine. We also illustrate two of our early examples of bone marrow edema detection using this technique, demonstrating that this technique successfully identified areas of bone marrow edema and were concordant with MRI findings.

articles.title: Conformal Uncertainty for Preoperative MRI Radiomic Glioma Subtyping: Showing When the Model Cannot Separate Subtypes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: MRI radiomic models predict WHO 2021 glioma subtypes with high AUCs, but reporting only the most probable subtype (argmax) can miss the less common oligodendroglioma. We evaluated whether class-conditional conformal prediction, which sets a separate probability cutoff for each subtype, lets a radiomic model return a set of plausible subtypes for each patient before tissue diagnosis, hypothesizing that it would cover all three subtypes at the target rate at the cost of larger sets. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1544 patients with preoperative T1, T2, contrast-enhanced T1, and FLAIR MRI from four public datasets. A random forest trained on TCGA and UCSF-PDGM (n=611) was applied unchanged to the Erasmus Glioma Database (EGD, n=404) and UTSW-Glioma (n=529), each split 200 times into a calibration half, used to fit every rule, and a test half. Class-conditional conformal prediction was compared with single-subtype rules, probability sets, abstention, and standard conformal prediction (one shared cutoff). Rules were compared on per-subtype coverage (the share of patients whose set contained the true subtype), mean set size, and the share of patients given a single subtype and its accuracy. RESULTS: Per-subtype AUCs were 0.87-0.96 (EGD) and 0.82-0.91 (UTSW-Glioma), yet argmax identified 7 of 73 and 4 of 63 oligodendrogliomas. At the 90% target, only class-conditional conformal prediction reached it for all three subtypes in both cohorts (mean coverage 0.90-0.93, mean set size 1.39 and 1.70). Standard conformal prediction covered 0.51 and 0.37 of oligodendrogliomas, probability sets fell below the target for two subtypes in UTSW-Glioma, and abstention matched on single-subtype calls needed larger sets (1.79 and 2.17). Single-subtype sets, given to 61.8% and 41.7% of patients, were correct in 98.5% and 97.4% when they named glioblastoma but about half the time otherwise. Development-cohort cutoffs fell below the target for glioblastoma (0.84 and 0.79). CONCLUSIONS: Class-conditional conformal prediction allowed the model to suggest multiple glioma subtypes when uncertain, reducing the risk of excluding the correct diagnosis, particularly oligodendroglioma. With calibration using comparable patient populations, the correct subtype was included at the intended rate. Single-subtype predictions were most reliable for glioblastoma.

articles.title: Association Between FLAIR Vascular Hyperintensities and Angiographic Collateral Status in Acute MCA Occlusion.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The clinical significance of Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) vascular hyperintensities (FVHs) in acute ischemic stroke remains debated, particularly regarding their relationship with leptomeningeal collateral circulation. We aimed to assess the association between FVHs on baseline MRI and angiographic collateral status evaluated by digital subtraction angiography (DSA) in patients with middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients treated between 2010 to 2018 for an acute ischemic stroke due to isolated M1 MCA occlusion from two cohorts. All patients underwent baseline MRI with FLAIR sequences and pre-treatment DSA. FVHs were assessed using two approaches: a topographic score (FVH-ASPECTS) and a semi-quantitative score based on the number of axial FLAIR slices showing at least one FVH (FVH-slices). Collateral status was graded using the ASITN/SIR scale and dichotomized as poor (grades 0-2) or good (grades 3-4). Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlation, nonparametric tests, and logistic regression. Technical sensitivity analyses accounted for slice thickness and interslice spacing. Interreader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. RESULTS: Fifty-two patients were included. FVH-slices showed moderate-to-good interreader agreement (ICC = 0.77), whereas FVH-ASPECTS had lower reproducibility (ICC = 0.34). FVH-slices was weakly correlated with the full ASITN/SIR scale (ρ = 0.27, P = .053) and was higher in patients with good collaterals (P = .021). In univariable logistic regression, each 1-point increase was associated with higher odds of good collateral status (OR = 1.30; 95% CI, 1.00-1.70), but this association was attenuated after accounting for acquisition parameters. FVH-ASPECTS correlated with the full ASITN/SIR scale (ρ = 0.30, P = .029) but was not significantly associated with dichotomized collateral status. Neither FVH score nor ASITN/SIR grade was associated with 3-month functional outcome. CONCLUSIONS: FVH-slices was more reproducible than FVH-ASPECTS and showed a weak positive association with angiographic collateral status. However, attenuation after technical adjustment and the limited sample size indicate that these exploratory findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Assessment of Ankle Instability in Acute ATFL Tears using a Validated and Easy Ultrasound Technique.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the value of clinical versus ultrasound stress testing in ankle sprains. MATERIALS AND METHODS: All acute ankle sprain patients from 2015 to 2023 received threefold early and final clinical and ultrasound examinations, including stress testing, in a prospective cohort study. RESULTS: In 342 patients, ligament injuries were diagnosed by sonography: 192 (56.1%) ligamentous anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) tears, 111 (32.5%) osseous ATFL avulsions, 24 (7.0%) calcaneocuboid ligament tears, and 15 (4.4%) anterior tibiofibular ligament tears. Then, 117 patients with a complete ATFL tear were carefully further assessed with dynamic ultrasound. Hemarthros was found in 88.2%, and clinical tenderness at the ATFL in 89.1%. Clinical stress tests were only positive in 60.2%, but the talar shift of the injured side during stress ultrasound was Ø 3.9 mm (SD 0.19 mm), compared to 0.6 mm (SD 0.10 mm) on the uninjured side. Clinical accuracy compared to ultrasound stress testing was 66-70%, sensitivity 64-70%, and specificity 72-100%. Follow-up in 110 patients after 6 weeks of conservative treatment showed the talar shift of the injured side at 0.8 mm SD 0.95, indicating regained stability in 103 of 110 cases. CONCLUSION: Effusion/possibly hemarthros in sonography reliably indicates a ligament injury. Almost all ATFL tears exhibit instability, which clinical tests alone often fail to detect. The sonographic examination technique described here forms a practicable, immediate, nonpainful, measurable, validated, and reliable basis and yields sufficient accuracy to inform optimal therapeutic steps and ensure healing through regained stability. Ultrasound stability testing, therefore, should be implemented as the gold standard in the diagnostic process.

articles.title: Superior frontal and precentral atlas label contact and naturalistic saccade amplitude across geometric estimators.
articles.abstract: We explored whether MRI-derived geometry near the superior frontal-precentral sulcal junction differs between hemispheres and relates to naturalistic saccade amplitude. Structural MRI was available for 38 adults, and 37 had usable eye tracking during movie viewing. We compared two measurements of contact between atlas-defined sulcal regions: the length of their reconstructed shared border and the summed lengths of mesh edges that cross between them. The primary reconstructed-border measure did not provide statistically significant evidence of hemispheric asymmetry or an association with saccade amplitude after correction for the two principal tests. The amplitude estimate was negative (Spearman ρ = -.336; unadjusted bootstrap 95% confidence interval -.566 to -.045; Holm-adjusted P = .084). The crossing-edge measure showed a stronger association, but represents a different geometric quantity. Additional analyses examined mesh resolution, normalization, eye-tracking processing, movie segment, recording quality, anatomical comparison regions, and other saccade characteristics. The additional kinematic associations were nonsignificant after correction. Estimates depended on measurement choices, and regional specificity was not established. The primary analysis therefore did not establish an association between the reconstructed anatomical measure and naturalistic saccade amplitude. This exploratory study illustrates how the definition of an MRI-derived measure can affect brain-behavior results. A nonsignificant result does not demonstrate the absence of an association. Independent anatomical validation and replication with participant-specific functional localization are needed.

articles.title: Regional brain T2 relaxation time changes during neuropathic pain chronification: a longitudinal study in a rat model of orofacial pain.
articles.abstract: Trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) is an insidious form of chronic pain and current treatments are often ineffective reflecting an incomplete understanding of the biological processes. Whilst cross-sectional human studies have demonstrated structural and functional changes in multiple components of the pain-processing network, they cannot determine when these changes emerge during progression from injury to chronic pain. The primary aim of this study was to track T2 relaxation time changes as indicators of microstructural changes during TNP development following infra-orbital nerve chronic constriction injury (ION-CCI) in rats. Multi-echo T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans were acquired 7-days prior to injury and then at +2, +7, +14, and +28 days, in male ION-CCI (n=11), sham-injured (n=6), and naïve (n=8) groups. T2-relaxation time maps were used to identify early- and late-onset changes in T2 relaxation times over the entire brain and within the ascending pain pathway. Early after injury, transient, T2 relaxation time increases within the periaqueductal gray matter, ventroposterior thalamus and primary somatosensory cortex. In contrast, late-stage changes occurred in multiple components of the trigeminal pain pathway, including the spinal trigeminal nucleus and tract as well as in sensory, affective and cognitive processing regions such as the hypothalamus, entorhinal cortex, retrosplenial cortex, insula and secondary somatosensory cortex. Many of these late T2 alterations occurred in regions previously shown to undergo volumetric changes and astrogliosis in the same animals. These findings reveal early dynamic T2 relaxation time changes of ascending trigeminal pain pathways followed by sustained alterations across trigeminal brainstem nuclei, limbic-hypothalamic systems, and higher-order cortical networks.

articles.title: Echo-time dependence of apparent microstructural metrics in diffusion MRI.
articles.abstract: Diffusion MRI metrics acquired at a single echo time are apparent, relaxation-weighted estimates. TE-associated variation may reflect differences in transverse relaxation weighting among water pools. We systematically quantified this variation across diffusion models, tissue classes, and pathological contexts.Approach: Multi-shell diffusion MRI was acquired at seven echo times (75-135 ms) in 68 participants. The cohort included 11 healthy controls and 57 patients with neurological disorders. We reconstructed 38 metrics from 9 diffusion models at each echo time. The primary inferential analysis estimated linear slopes for each participant across 38 metrics and five tissues. We tested slopes against zero and compared them between tissues using a global Bonferroni correction. Exploratory analyses evaluated cross-grade patterns in 13 patients with World Health Organization grade II-IV glioma and local responses in 14 lesion masks.Main results: Echo-time sensitivity was widespread and depended on model, tissue, and pathological context. After global Bonferroni correction, 170 of 190 metric-tissue slopes differed from zero, and 300 of 380 tissue comparisons were significant. Under the primary full-shell DTI configuration, DTI-derived diffusivities generally decreased with echo time, DTI diffusivity slope directions depended strongly on shell selection, with low-b fitting reversing the MD and RD slopes in all five tissue classes. FWDTI diffusivities also generally decreased with echo time. Kurtosis metrics and metrics reflecting tissue complexity generally increased, particularly in the brainstem. Orientation dispersion index was comparatively stable. Exploratory pathological analyses showed nonmonotonic cross-grade patterns and heterogeneous lesion responses.Significance: Single-TE diffusion MRI metrics are apparent, relaxation-weighted estimates. Their TE dependence may reflect compartment-specific transverse relaxation and other acquisition- and tissue-related factors. TE should be reported and its effects assessed in quantitative diffusion MRI, with appropriate modeling or harmonization when comparing measurements across protocols, sites, time points, tissues, and pathological conditions.

articles.title: Anatomical deformation modes: a compact scalar-mode subspace for patient-specific deformation modeling.
articles.abstract: Objective To develop a patient-specific motion-modeling framework that represents a dense three-dimensional deformation vector field (DVF) as a linear combination of scalar-field bases, termed anatomical deformation modes (ADM), with vector coefficients.Approach We formulated ADM as a low-dimensional parameterization of the DVF and showed that it generalizes the vector mode (VM) representation at matched spatial-map storage and provides pose invariance. Patient-specific ADM can be either extracted by principal component analysis (PCA) of the component fields of multiple DVFs or predicted from a single CT image by a deep neural network as a population-learned, anatomy-conditioned prior. From sparse 2D or 3D observations, the coefficients, and thus the dense DVF, are recovered by an iterative Gauss-Newton coefficient solver with closed-form linear updates for images and masks, or a single linear least-squares solve for surface points.Main results On a public 4D-lung CT dataset with pTVReg-derived reference DVFs, ADM achieved a 95th-percentile endpoint error (EPE-P95) of 1.25-1.56 mm versus 1.34-1.62 mm for VM at matched spatial-map storage. A single PCA-derived mode reached EPE-P95 2.48 mm against the reference DVFs on the 3 mm grid, a one-scalar-map budget unavailable to VM. Without retraining, network-predicted ADM supported four CT-derived simulated observation types relevant to real-time guidance (3D images, 2D images, 2D masks and surface points), and one or two modes reduced mean EPE-P95 by 20-31% relative to no registration. Online coefficient fitting required 1.36-3.77 ms for 2D images and masks and 0.044 ms for surface points on an RTX 4090.Significance Patient-specific deformation models can thus be built from multiple DVFs when prior motion images are available or from a single static CT image before any motion imaging. By encoding patient-specific anatomical and spatial constraints, ADM supports the development of fast, observation-flexible methods for recovering dense deformation from controlled sparse observations.

articles.title: Biophysical model-based deep learning denoising for stabilized IMPULSED dMRI microenvironment parameter fitting.
articles.abstract: Diffusion-weighted MRI (dMRI) is a powerful tool for quantifying cellular microenvironment parameters. However, the inherently low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of dMRI can compromise the accuracy and reliability of parameter estimation. This study proposes a {\rev biophysical model}-based deep learning (DL) denoising framework designed to enhance dMRI signal quality and improve the robustness of subsequent biophysical model fitting, with potential relevance to low-SNR settings such as clinical 1.5 T MRI acquisitions.Approach. A dataset of paired noise-free and Rician-noise-corrupted dMRI signals was generated using the IMPULSED-dMRI signal model. Three denoising architectures were evaluated: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Denoised signals were then fitted to estimate cell diameter $d$, intracellular volume fraction $V_{\mathrm{in}}$, and extracellular apparent diffusion coefficient $D_\mathrm{ex}$. Performance was assessed using signal-domain Mean Absolute Error (MAE), fitted-parameter MAE, and {\rev boundary solution rate} in synthetic IMPULSED-dMRI data with known ground-truth parameters and in \textit{in vitro} evaluation using HeLa and MC38 cell lines.Main results. DL-based processing substantially improved dMRI signal denoising. {\rev The MLP and LSTM achieved comparable denoising performance, and both outperformed the CNN.} Averaged across all signals, the LSTM reduced denoising MAE from 5.97\% to 1.58\%. In the subsequent model fitting step, the LSTM produced modest reductions in parameter MAE, from $5.34 \, \mu\text{m}$ to $4.02 \, \mu\text{m}$ for $d$, from 15.00\% to 11.96\% for $V_\mathrm{in}$, and from $0.77$ to $0.63 \, \mu\text{m}^2/\text{ms}$ for $D_\mathrm{ex}$. The dominant benefit was fitting stabilization, with the overall {\rev boundary solution rate} reduced from 57.6\% to 17.7\%. In \textit{in vitro} experiments, relative to experimental references, the LSTM reduced MAE from $2.1 \, \mu\text{m}$ to $0.4 \, \mu\text{m}$ for $d$ and from 7.8 to 5.4 percentage points for $V_\mathrm{in}$, while reducing the mean overall {\rev boundary solution rate} from 17.7\% to 0\%.Significance.The proposed framework improves dMRI signal quality and stabilizes subsequent IMPULSED-based microenvironmental parameter fitting. The primary value of this approach is improved fitting reliability under noisy dMRI conditions, with secondary gains in parameter accuracy, and it warrants further validation in heterogeneous tissues and \textit{in vivo} datasets.

articles.title: Detector-side neural timing calibration for TOF-PET from coincidence supervision.
articles.abstract: Machine-learning methods can model non-linear event-dependent timing effects in time-of-flight positron emission tomography (TOF-PET), but calibration measurements naturally provide timing supervision only at the coincidence-level rather than for individual detector interactions. We investigate whether coincidence measurements can be used to learn reusable detector-side timing calibration functions without individually labelled interaction times.Approach: A shared detector-conditioned neural network independently processes each single-event readout and predicts a detector-side timing correction and variance contribution. During training, two detector-side timing estimates are differenced and compared with the geometrically expected time difference obtained from point-source coincidence measurements. We evaluate the method on three heterogeneous PET systems against conventional time-skew and time-walk calibration and matched direct coincidence-level neural models.Main results: Under a common energy-window setting, the proposed model reduced coincidence timing resolution from 321.7 to 263.0ps, 462.4 to 431.7ps, and 417.0 to 382.0ps relative to charge-based time-walk correction on the three systems. In detector-pair holdout experiments, detector-side models achieved comparable or slightly better timing performance than direct coincidence-level neural models while retaining independently applicable singles-level outputs. The learned calibration generalized to unseen source positions and detector pairs, enabled recombination of independently trained scanner components after scalar timing-reference alignment, provided event-wise coincidence-timing uncertainty stratification in both full-ring systems, and remained compatible with low-precision inference after quantization-aware training.Significance: Coincidence supervision enables reusable detector-side timing corrections that improve CTR without single-event timing labels. This preserves a singles-level calibration interface while enabling machine-learning-based nonlinear timing correction, modular scanner calibration, and event-specific coincidence-timing uncertainty estimates.

articles.title: Influence of pulse shape and coil orientation on TMS activation patterns using biophysical axon models.
articles.abstract: Despite the clinical prevalence of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), the precise relationship between stimulation parameters and the resulting activation patterns of the axons remains elusive, particularly regarding the interaction between pulse waveforms and coil orientations. Approach. We developed a computational model that combines magnetic resonance image (MRI), white matter tractography, electric field analysis, and biophysical axon models. Using this computational framework, ten publicly available TMS pulse shapes-categorised into monophasic, half-sine, and biphasic waveforms-were evaluated across a 360° range of coil orientations. Focusing specifically on posterior-anterior (PA), anterior-posterior (AP), lateral-medial (LM), and medial-lateral (ML) directions, the model predicted activation intensities and activation sites within the hand area of the primary motor cortex (M1). Main results. Simulated activation intensity ratios matched empirical data from the literature. Excitation using monophasic AP-TMS requires higher electric field intensity compared to PA-TMS. Specifically, AP-TMS activation sites are predicted to be more distal from M1, often occurring in the postcentral gyrus or underneath the central sulcus. Axons are more likely activated under the pulse's negative phase using half sine and biphasic waveforms. Higher threshold is required for activation at LM and ML coil orientations according to model prediction. Significance. Our computational model can be used to generate hypotheses regarding the effect of pulse waveforms and coil orientations against the measurements and observations; and it may assist users to select coil orientations and intensities of TMS for different stimulation targets.

articles.title: PRISM: a physics-informed spatiotemporal convolutional network for interaction localisation in continuous annular nanocomposite PET scintillators.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Continuous annular positron emission tomography (PET) detectors moulded from nanocomposite scintillators such as LaF 3 :Ce in polystyrene could substantially reduce fabrication cost relative to discrete-crystal arrays, but strong optical (Rayleigh) scattering and coincidence label ambiguity make recovery of the first point of interaction (FPoI) a severely ill-posed inverse problem. We investigated whether embedding scanner topology and coincidence physics into the network itself renders it tractable. APPROACH: PRISM (Physics-informed Regression of Interactions in Scintillating Monoliths) is a spatiotemporal convolutional network that treats dual-surface photodetector readout as a short burst of time-binned cylindrical intensity maps (five 10 ns frames). It applies circular padding azimuthally to respect cylindrical topology, injects positional and radial depth-ratio channels, and is trained with a virtual cylinder-aware loss combining permutation-invariant coincidence regression with boundary constraints and a polar-weighted auxiliary term. A LaF 3 :Ce/polystyrene scanner (42.9 mm mean radial thickness, 296 mm axial field of view) was modelled in OpenGATE; 8 587 880 18 F decays yielded 735 230 labelled bursts. MAIN RESULTS: On a held-out set, PRISM achieved a median three-dimensional FPoI error of 8.26 mm (mean 10.33 mm; 90th percentile 19.4 mm), a threefold reduction relative to physics-agnostic backbones under an identical input representation (ResNet-18: 25.61 mm median), with fewer trainable parameters. Restricting evaluation to the inner half of the annulus reduced the median to 6.67 mm. SIGNIFICANCE: Embedding cylindrical continuity and coincidence-permutation invariance materially improves localisation in strongly scattering monolithic annular detectors, supporting the feasibility of low-cost continuous-shell nanocomposite PET.

articles.title: A multi-scale extension of the oxygen effect-incorporated stochastic microdosimetric kinetic model for FLASH radiotherapy: unifying radiochemical pathways and macroscopic inter-track saturation.
articles.abstract: Objective This study aims to develop a unified biophysical framework to resolve prevailing paradoxes in FLASH radiotherapy, including normoxic protection, high-LET sparing, and phenotypic variability, which macroscopic radiochemical models cannot consistently explain.Approach We established the Multi-Scale Oxygen effect-incorporated Stochastic Microdosimetric Kinetic (MS-OSMK) model utilizing an Event-by-Event formalism. This framework integrates radiolytic oxygen depletion (ROD, characterized by depletion rate g), radical recombination (RR), and introduces a novel macroscopic inter-track saturation mechanism (threshold D_"sat" ). Model parameters were optimized via global simultaneous fitting to clonogenic survival datasets. A rigorous ablation study employing the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and newly developed phase-space visualizations, namely sparing advantage and mechanistic contribution maps, was conducted to isolate specific drivers.Main results The comprehensive MS-OSMK model achieved the lowest AIC, statistically validating the necessity of integrating physical and chemical pathways. Contribution maps revealed profound phenotypic dependence: protection in low-metabolic HDF cells (g=0.00 "mmHg\/Gy" ) was strictly governed by oxygen-independent physical saturation (D_"sat" =8.2 "Gy" ), whereas highly oxidative HSG cells (g=2.00 "mmHg\/Gy" ) were driven by a robust ROD-saturation synergy (D_"sat" =1.7 "Gy" ). Furthermore, advantage maps visually quantified that significant normoxic sparing mathematically necessitates dual thresholds: ultra-high dose rates and large fractional doses (≧10 "Gy" ). By decoupling intra-track overkill from macroscopic saturation, the model successfully resolved the high-LET paradox.Significance The MS-OSMK model provides a robust computational foundation that resolves major FLASH paradoxes without non-physical parameterization. It reveals that the FLASH effect is not a universal "normal-tissue advantage" but a highly dynamic, phenotype-dependent synergy of physical and chemical mechanisms, thereby establishing a rigorous theoretical basis for future clinical translation.

articles.title: Nauta type IV cystic meningioma in a child.
Cross-Sectional observational study of imaging findings in patients presenting with chronic non-bacterial osteomyelitis in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic non-infectious osteomyelitis (CNO) is a rare condition that presents with multifocal inflammation of bone in children and adolescents. The exact distribution, severity and identifiable patterns of disease are not fully understood. OBJECTIVES: Describe the prevalence and pattern of radiological abnormalities present at the time of diagnosis in patients with chronic non-bacterial osteitis. MATERIALS & METHODS: Multi-centre national prospective cross-sectional observational study set in the United Kingdom. Patients with new diagnoses of CNO were recruited between 2020-2022. MRI was reviewed independently by two radiologists and disagreements were resolved by a panel of three. The anatomical location for each lesion was recorded by bone and within bone. The severity of the MRI findings was scored using CROMRIS. Hypothesis testing and agglomerative k-cluster analysis was used to identify patterns of disease. RESULTS: A total of 246 imaging studies were retrieved for 138 patients (87 female, 51 male, median age 10.5 years, IQR 9.0, 12.6) comprising 96 Whole Body MRI (WBMR), 67 MRI, 61 radiographic and 20 CT studies. Median time from diagnosis to imaging was -16 days (IQR -110, 14). In all 581 foci of disease were identified (inter-rater agreement 81.4%) most commonly affecting the pelvis and lower limb (62%). The clavicle was the 5th most common location but the most common single site location (9%) for single site disease. Abnormal vertebrae were identified in 55 patients (38%) and these were complicated by a fracture in 30%. There was no difference in the prevalence of abnormalities between the sexes. Patients with vertebral involvement had fewer sites of disease. Involvement of the head and mandible is often isolated. Four out of five lesions on WBMR were discordant with the patients' symptoms and 56% of all sites of disease were discordant. CONCLUSION: The pelvis and lower limb are the most common locations affected by CNO. Vertebral involvement is more common than previously reported and clinically silent disease is common. Apart from disease in the mandible and head there are no other discernible radiological phenotypes.

articles.title: National Comprehensive Cancer Network: The Room Where It Happens.
Should whole body CT be the default imaging technique in trauma?
articles.abstract: Hospital presentations secondary to trauma are increasing in the United Kingdom, which presents challenges to imaging services. Whole body CT (WBCT) has been adopted widely, allowing rapid assessment of patients, and faster transit through the emergency department. There remains debate as to whether this practice also improves patient outcomes. There are potential drawbacks to WBCT use including, detection of incidental findings and potential false reassurance. WBCT should not be the default investigation for patients who have suffered traumatic injuries. Future research should aim to clarify which patient subgroups may benefit from this imaging technique.

articles.title: Hidden Pitfalls of artificial intelligence in pediatric emergency radiology: a pictorial review of failure modes, clinical implications, and mitigation strategies.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming diagnostic radiology, yet its current clinical application in pediatric imaging remains fraught with challenges. Considerations that are unique to pediatric patients, including vast variations in developmental anatomy, age-specific disease patterns and pathologies, and technical variability create diagnostic challenges for which many commercially available AI systems, trained predominantly on adult data, are ill-equipped. This review utilizes literature evidence and illustrative clinical cases to critically examine various weaknesses of AI in pediatric imaging. Common pitfalls include misclassification of normal developmental variants, inability to distinguish pathological mimics, vulnerability to motion artifacts, modality-specific limitations, and errors introduced by artifacts or confounders. These failures are amplified by limited pediatric training data, annotation bias, and lack of contextual integration. We propose a structured framework for mitigating these risks, including pediatric-specific data curation, contextual model adaptation, algorithmic transparency, integrated feedback systems, technologist training, case-appropriate sedation planning, and centralized error tracking. These interventions are essential to enable safe, reliable, and ethically responsible AI deployment in pediatric emergency radiology.
